subject: International Law
title: 16. War, Armed Conflicts and Other Hostilities

segments.text: This topic connects the legal status of hostilities with rules on participants, conduct, occupation, detention and termination of conflict.
Use modern “armed conflict” terminology rather than assuming a formal declaration of war is necessary. Connect the topic to IHL while keeping it distinct from use-of-force law.

Modern international law increasingly uses the term 'armed conflict' because IHL applies according to factual and legal thresholds rather than a formal declaration of war. A state of war may have historical and domestic-law significance, but absence of a declaration does not prevent IHL from applying once an armed conflict exists.

The legal consequences of armed conflict extend beyond targeting. They can affect detention, treatment of prisoners, occupation, protection of civilians, neutral relations, diplomatic and economic measures, and the operation of treaties.

Belligerent occupation exists when territory is actually placed under the authority of a hostile army and the occupying power can exercise that authority. Occupation does not transfer sovereignty. The law of occupation regulates the temporary administration of the territory and seeks to protect the population while recognizing limited security powers.

An armed conflict can end through cessation of hostilities, armistice, peace agreement or factual termination depending on the legal context. Some IHL obligations continue after active fighting ends, especially regarding detainees, missing persons, mines, remains and accountability.

blocks.text: Relationship with other bodies of law

segments.text: Human-rights law does not simply disappear during armed conflict, although the relationship between human-rights obligations and IHL can raise questions of lex specialis, derogation and jurisdiction. International criminal law may impose individual responsibility for serious violations, while state responsibility addresses international wrongs attributable to states.

items.text: Modern international law focuses on the factual existence of armed conflict rather than requiring a formal declaration of war before humanitarian rules can apply.

Conflict classification determines which body of IHL rules governs the relationship. International armed conflicts involve states in the relevant legal sense; non-international armed conflicts involve sustained hostilities meeting the legal threshold within a state or across related situations.

Occupation, detention, treatment of protected persons and conduct of hostilities are legal consequences that arise from the factual and legal situation, not merely from political labels used by the parties.

Termination of active hostilities and formal peace arrangements can be different moments. Legal effects may continue after fighting stops, especially regarding detainees, occupation or unresolved obligations.

rows: Common confusion to avoid: Do not make the legal application of IHL depend on whether the parties call the situation a “war.” Classification is based on legal facts.
